Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a clean draft of the renewal package (MSA + order form) with the proposed term shift and capacity uplift. High level:
- Term: proposed move from 12 months to 24 months (to lock in current pricing tiers)
- Capacity: 2x baseline starting on the renewal effective date, with an 8-week phased ramp
- Commercial ask: 10% discount on unit price for the extended term

Can you review the draft and circulate any redlines from procurement/ops? If HelioGrid prefers we can present a compromise term (e.g., 18 months) — open to alignment. Ideally we get redlines back by EOD 2028-04-29 so legal can triage before the month close.

Evelyn,

Thanks for the draft. We reviewed with procurement and legal. A few quick items from our side:
- Term: procurement is reluctant to move to 24 months given our budgeting cycle — they prefer to stay at 12 months.
- Billing: we need clarity on prorated billing for the phased ramp; please confirm how charges are calculated during ramp weeks.
- SLA: we requested a written SLA credit cap for prolonged latency incidents (they asked for a 45-day backstop).

I attached our redlines (Hg_Redlines_20280426.docx) with inline comments. Two asks: (1) can Redwood share headroom reporting for the last quarter to justify the 2x uplift request; (2) can we see a sample order form showing phased ramp pricing applied?

We can be flexible on term if there's an intermediate option, but procurement will need the finance team sign-off.

Hi Maria — thanks for the prompt review and the redlines. I reviewed the Hg_Redlines_20280426.docx and want to propose a compromise we think will close more quickly:

Proposed compromise (Redwood legal + sales):
- Term: 18 months (midpoint between teams)
- Pricing: 10% unit discount applied across the 18-month term; phased ramp billed at actual usage with a guaranteed effective floor of 60% of uplift price during ramp weeks (to avoid supply-side inefficiencies)
- Billing/proration: charges calculated on daily usage; we will provide a worked example in the order form appendix
- SLA: we can accept an SLA credit cap aligned with our standard SLO policy; however, we cannot commit to a 45-day backstop — propose standard credit calculation (hours of downtime x hourly rate) with a maximum credit equal to one month's spend for the affected resource class
- Data & retention: no change to data retention language in the MSA

If HelioGrid agrees in principle to 18 months and the billing approach above, Redwood can re-issue a tracked redline package today and route a DocuSign link for signature.

Attachment: Proposed_18mo_Compromise_20280427.pdf (summary with example calculations).

Evelyn — looping Ben for the signature path and any commercial flex.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
